en: Could you please resend the invoice in PDF?
tamil: இன்வாய்ஸை PDF-ல திருப்பி அனுப்ப முடியுமா?
explain: 'Resend' means send again. 'In PDF' means in that file format.
usage: Use it in formal emails with clients and vendors.
leelaQ: What file formats do you know?
answer: I know PDF, Word and Excel.

en: Please keep your phone away from the exam hall.
tamil: தயவுசெஞ்சு உங்க போனை தேர்வு அறைக்கு வெளியில வெச்சிடுங்க.
explain: 'Keep away from' means do not bring near.
usage: A rule said in schools, colleges and offices.
leelaQ: Where do you keep your phone while studying?
answer: I keep it in another room.

en: Excuse me, how do I connect to this printer?
tamil: மன்னிக்கணும், இந்த பிரிண்டர்ல எப்படி கனெக்ட் பண்றது?
explain: 'Excuse me' starts a polite question.
usage: Use it in a new office or a shop.
leelaQ: What do you print at work?
answer: I print reports and tickets.

en: I do not understand how this app works.
tamil: இந்த ஆப் எப்படி வேலை செய்யுதுன்னு எனக்கு புரியல.
explain: 'How this app works' is a noun clause: the word order is like a statement.
usage: Say it to a helper or in a review when an app is confusing.
leelaQ: What do you do when you cannot use a new app?
answer: I watch a short video or ask a friend.

en: He never turns off his notifications, so his phone keeps buzzing.
tamil: அவன் நோட்டிபிகேஷன்களை ஆஃப் பண்ணவே மாட்டான், அதனால அவன் போன் அடிச்சுக்கிட்டே இருக்கும்.
explain: 'Never' is a frequency word with a negative meaning.
usage: Use it jokingly about a friend who is always on the phone.
leelaQ: Do you get many notifications?
answer: Yes, I get too many, so I turned off some.

en: I did not know that you can mute a chat group.
tamil: க்ரூப் சாட்டை மியூட் பண்ணலாம்னு எனக்குத் தெரியாது.
context: Learning a tip from a friend.
explain: 'Did not know' is the past negative.
usage: Say it when someone teaches you a new phone tip.
leelaQ: What new phone tip did you learn recently?
answer: I learned how to scan documents with my phone.

en: My phone does not turn on after the update.
tamil: அப்டேட் பண்ணின பிறகு என் போன் ஆன் ஆகல.
context: Reporting a problem at a service centre.
explain: 'Does not' is used with he, she and it.
usage: Say it at a service centre when a phone stops working.
leelaQ: What would you do if your phone does not turn on?
answer: I would charge it and then take it to a service centre.

en: I can't log in because the system says my password is wrong.
tamil: நான் லாக் இன் பண்ண முடியல, ஏன்னா என் பாஸ்வேர்டு தப்புன்னு சிஸ்டம் சொல்லுது.
explain: 'Can't' is the short form of 'cannot'.
usage: Say it to the IT team in an office.
leelaQ: Do you use the same password everywhere?
answer: No, I use different passwords for different sites.

en: No, I have not downloaded that app.
tamil: இல்ல, நான் அந்த ஆப்பை டவுன்லோட் பண்ணல.
explain: A short negative answer can start with 'No'.
usage: Use it as a clear, polite answer in a conversation.
leelaQ: Which apps have you not tried yet?
answer: I have not tried any food delivery app yet.

en: The meeting will not start until everyone joins.
tamil: எல்லாரும் வர்ற வரைக்கும் மீட்டிங் தொடங்காது.
explain: 'Until' means up to the time that something happens.
usage: A host says it when people are still waiting.
leelaQ: What do you do while waiting for a meeting?
answer: I check my emails or talk to colleagues.

en: I will not use my phone while driving.
tamil: நான் வண்டி ஓட்டும்போது போன் யூஸ் பண்ண மாட்டேன்.
explain: 'Will not' makes a firm promise. 'While driving' shows two actions together.
usage: Say it to family to show you follow road safety.
leelaQ: Why should we not use phones while driving?
answer: It is dangerous and can cause accidents.

en: Our website is not secure, so we are fixing it now.
tamil: எங்க வெப்சைட் பாதுகாப்பா இல்ல, அதனால இப்போ சரி பண்றோம்.
context: IT staff explaining to a manager.
explain: 'Secure' means safe from danger.
usage: Use it at work in IT updates and reports.
leelaQ: Why is a secure website important?
answer: It keeps people's information safe.

en: I have not checked my social media today.
tamil: நான் இன்னைக்கு என் சோஷியல் மீடியாவை பாக்கல.
context: Telling a friend about your day.
explain: 'Today' shows the day is not finished, so use present perfect.
usage: Use it in casual talk about screen time.
leelaQ: How often do you check social media?
answer: I check it a few times a day.

en: Do you think it is a good idea to buy a second-hand phone?
tamil: செகண்ட்-ஹேண்ட் போன் வாங்குறது நல்ல யோசனைன்னு நினைக்கிறியா?
explain: 'Do you think...?' asks for an opinion.
usage: Ask a friend or a seller before you buy a used device.
leelaQ: What are the good points of a second-hand phone?
answer: It is cheaper, but the battery may be weak.

en: Where did you buy this laptop bag?
tamil: இந்த லேப்டாப் பேக்கை எங்க வாங்கின?
explain: 'Where did you buy...?' asks about a place in the past.
usage: Ask in casual talk about gadgets.
leelaQ: Where do you keep your laptop?
answer: I keep it in a bag on my study table.

en: Is there any shop nearby that repairs phones?
tamil: பக்கத்துல போன் ரிப்பேர் பண்ற கடை ஏதாவது இருக்கா?
explain: 'Is there any...?' asks if something exists nearby.
usage: Ask a local person or a security guard when your phone breaks in a new place.
leelaQ: How do you find a good repair shop?
answer: I ask my friends and read reviews online.

en: I just bought a new smart watch, and it tracks my steps.
tamil: நான் இப்போதான் ஒரு புது ஸ்மார்ட் வாட்ச் வாங்கினேன், அது என் நடையை கணக்கு வெக்குது.
context: Showing a friend a new gadget.
explain: 'Just' shows something happened a moment ago. 'Tracks' means keeps a record.
usage: Say it when you show off or explain a gadget.
leelaQ: Would you like to wear a smart watch?
answer: Yes, I would like one to count my steps.

en: The hotel Wi-Fi works well, but the signal is weak in the corridor.
tamil: ஹோட்டல் வைஃபை நல்லா வேலை செய்யுது, ஆனா காரிடார்ல சிக்னல் வீக்கா இருக்கு.
context: Giving feedback at a hotel desk.
explain: 'But' joins two opposite ideas.
usage: Say it at a hotel reception when giving feedback.
leelaQ: Do you check the Wi-Fi when you stay in a hotel?
answer: Yes, I always ask about the Wi-Fi before booking.

en: My brother is playing a game on the tablet right now.
tamil: என் தம்பி இப்போ டேப்லெட்ல கேம் விளையாடிட்டு இருக்கான்.
context: Telling a guest why the tablet is busy.
explain: 'Right now' stresses that it is happening at this moment.
usage: Use it in casual talk at home.
leelaQ: What games do you play on your phone?
answer: I play puzzle games when I have free time.

en: We got a new router yesterday, and the speed is much better.
tamil: நாங்க நேத்து புது ரூட்டர் வாங்கினோம், இப்போ ஸ்பீடு ரொம்ப நல்லா இருக்கு.
context: Sharing good news about the internet at home.
explain: 'Much better' is a comparison that shows a big change.
usage: Say it to neighbours or relatives who ask about internet.
leelaQ: How fast is your internet?
answer: It is quite fast, so I can watch videos without waiting.

en: I will update my phone tonight when I get home.
tamil: நான் இன்னைக்கு ராத்திரி வீட்டுக்கு போனதும் என் போனை அப்டேட் பண்ணுவேன்.
explain: After 'when', use present simple even for the future.
usage: Say it when you decide to do a task later.
leelaQ: What will you do on your phone tonight?
answer: I will talk to my friends and watch a movie.

en: She has saved all my contact numbers on her new phone.
tamil: அவ என் எல்லா காண்டாக்ட் நம்பர்களையும் தன் புது போன்ல சேவ் பண்ணி வெச்சிருக்கா.
context: Talking about a sister or friend.
explain: 'Has saved' shows a finished action with a result now.
usage: Use it when you tell someone that your number is already with a person.
leelaQ: Do you remember phone numbers or save them?
answer: I save them because I cannot remember many numbers.

en: The speaker in this room has a loud echo.
tamil: இந்த ரூம்ல ஸ்பீக்கர்ல பெரிய எக்கோ வருது.
context: Telling the organiser about audio trouble.
explain: 'Echo' is the sound that repeats.
usage: Say it at a meeting room or a hall with sound problems.
leelaQ: Where have you heard a loud echo?
answer: I heard one in a big empty hall.

en: I usually pay my electricity bill through an app.
tamil: நான் பொதுவா என் கரண்ட் பில்லை ஆப் மூலமா கட்டுவேன்.
context: Telling a friend how you pay bills.
explain: 'Through' means by using something.
usage: Use it when you talk about easy online payments.
leelaQ: How do you pay your bills?
answer: I pay them on my phone using UPI.

en: I am waiting for the page to load.
tamil: நான் பேஜ் லோட் ஆகுறதுக்காக காத்துட்டு இருக்கேன்.
context: Telling someone why you are slow to respond.
explain: 'Waiting for' plus a noun and 'to' shows what you expect.
usage: Say it on a call or at a counter when a system is slow.
leelaQ: What do you do when a page loads slowly?
answer: I wait for a minute and then refresh it.
